concept: Guideline 2.1 Information Needed reply: review notes
summary: Source-anchored research for Guideline 2.1 Information Needed reply: review notes. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: 'Information Needed' is a provisional rejection under Guideline 2.1: App Review asks questions (costs, hardware, account creation, business model, login access) because it could not complete review; the developer answers in Resolution Center or in the App Review Information section of App Store Connect. (high confidence)

Many Information Needed rejections need no new build: after correcting the App Review Information (demo account, notes) the developer can reply in Resolution Center; a new binary is only needed if a code bug is the cause. (medium confidence)
Guideline 2.1(b) tells developers to explain in review notes any configured in-app purchase that the reviewer cannot find in the app. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

Unclear or evasive replies can trigger a slow secondary review; one author advises budgeting an extra 1-2 weeks when a reply is likely to prompt follow-up questions, so answer each question directly and completely. (medium confidence)

Effective review notes are short (3-5 lines), give concrete navigation to the features under review, list working credentials (no 2FA/email/SMS gate, not expired), explain features needing hardware the reviewer lacks, and avoid marketing copy; stale UI directions are a common pitfall. (medium confidence)

Guideline 2.1(a) requires final, fully functional submissions with complete metadata and working URLs, demo account info if the app has a login (with the back-end turned on), and permits a built-in demo mode in place of a demo account only with prior Apple approval; apps that crash or are incomplete are rejected. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

Apple's standard text for flagged apps says the app gets a longer review and is ineligible for expedited review until the developer confirms compliance; resubmitting without the requested confirmation keeps the longer review. (medium confidence)
Replies may be written in the developer's preferred language, and developers should avoid loose wording that raises extra concerns. (low confidence)
